headlines.full_text: الاتحاد الجزائري يُنهي رسميا تعاقده مع المدرب بيتكوفيتش أعلن الاتحاد الجزائري لكرة القدم يوم الاثنين إنهاء تعاقده مع مدرب المنتخب فلاديمير بيتكوفيتش وطاقمه الفني، وذلك باتفاق ودّي بين الطرفين. حفظ شارِكْ أعلن الاتحاد الجزائري لكرة القدم يوم الاثنين إنهاء تعاقده مع مدرب المنتخب فلاديمير بيتكوفيتش وطاقمه الفني، وذلك باتفاق ودّي بين الطرفين. وقال الاتحاد -في بيان- إن إنهاء العلاقة التعاقدية دخل حيز التنفيذ اعتبارا من الاثنين، دون أن يوضح الأسباب التي دفعته إلى هذا القرار. وأشاد الاتحاد بما وصفه باحترافية بيتكوفيتش وطاقمه الفني والتزامهم طوال فترة إشرافهم على المنتخب، مقدما لهم الشكر على العمل الذي أنجزوه خلال 29 شهرا قادوا فيها الفريق. وتمنى الاتحاد الجزائري للمدرب وأعضاء جهازه الفني التوفيق في مسيرتهم المهنية المقبلة، من دون أن يكشف عن هوية المدرب الذي سيتولى قيادة المنتخب خلال المرحلة القادمة. ويستعد منتخب الجزائر لخوض تصفيات كأس الأمم الأفريقية 2027 التي ستنطلق في سبتمبر/أيلول المقبل، إذ يتنافس مع زامبيا وتوغو وبوروندي في المجموعة التاسعة.

headlines.full_text: Раскрыта реакция США на визит американской делегации на ПМЭФ Реклама Глава КомиссииСШАпо изящным искусствам Родни Кук заявил, что американская сторона положительно оценила визит возглавляемой им делегации на Петербургский международный экономический форум (ПМЭФ) в июне текущего года. Он рассказал об этом в беседе сРИА Новости. По словам Кука, вВашингтоне«очень довольны» поездкой. Общую реакцию на свой визит он назвал «очень позитивной». «Госдепартаментразрешил мне поехать, выстроил программу визита, а его представители присутствовали на каждой встрече. Я воспринимаю это как позитивный шаг», — отметил Кук. В июне пресс-секретарь президента РоссииДмитрий Песков, комментируя приезд американской делегации на ПМЭФ,призвалне преувеличивать значения визита представителей США. Он указал, что в Вашингтоне увязывают все с урегулированием конфликта наУкраине.

headlines.full_text: The prisoner spoke about the cost of escaping from Ukraine without guarantees Реклама Побег сУкраинынелегальными путями можно организовать за пять тысяч долларов. При этом никто не дает гарантий того, что «покупатель» услуги сможет успешно пересечь границу. Об этом сообщил пленный изВооруженных сил Украины(ВСУ) Александр Борщук, его цитируетТАСС. По словам солдата, побег из республики организовывают черезМолдавию. «Цены разные, от пяти тысяч долларов и выше. Тебя доводят только [до украинской границы], а дальше как повезет», — рассказал он. Ранее другой военнопленныйрассказал, что солдаты ВСУ — как заключившие контракт, так и мобилизованные, — ежемесячно получают зарплату в размере 20 тысяч гривен (около 35,6 тысячи рублей).

headlines.full_text: 'My only son was shot standing up for justice' - inside city gripped by deadly protests in Pakistan-administered Kashmir The BBC gains unique access to Rawalakot, scene of violent clashes between security forces and protesters in Pakistan-administered Kashmir. Dr Anwar's makeshift clinic is not far from the main protest site in the city of Rawalakot in Pakistan-administered Kashmir (PAK). A spare bedroom acts as a medical supply cupboard, outside is a bed under a red stretched tarpaulin. Lying across the bed is Shafqat Hussain, shot in the chest. The sheet he lies on is already stained with the blood of previously injured. He is dying. In the last two months, dozens of people have been killed across the region in clashes between security officials and protesters from the group Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC). This region - home to about 4.5 million people -currently has elections taking place. The BBC is the first media organisation to gain access to Rawalakot and speak to those at the heart of the protests. Dr Anwar – whose name, like most of those in this report, has been changed to protect contributors – tells our team: "We have enough supplies to provide first aid. We can stop bleeding, clean and dress wounds, and remove superficial bullets. But patients with serious injuries to the chest, abdomen, head, or other vital organs need advanced hospitals." Anwar adds: "Even major hospitals would struggle if many such patients arrived at the same time." Since 27 July, the clinic has treated around 50 to 60 critically injured patients, the doctor says, adding that he personally treated 15 to 20 with gunshot wounds. headlines.full_text: Washington state fires destroy hundreds of buildings and force Spokane-area residents to evacuate Washington state fires destroy hundreds of buildings and force Spokane-area residents to evacuate SPOKANE, Wash. — Some residents returned to devastated neighborhoods ineastern Washington stateto find their homes leveled by wildfires that erupted across a parched landscape over the weekend, covering yards in charred debris. In some cases, only chimneys were left standing. The fires in and around Spokane, the state’s second-largest city, had burned about 12.5 square miles by Monday and filled the sky with smoke and haze. Light winds and lower temperatures arrived to help firefighters, but at least 600 buildings had been destroyed and some 67,000 people were under evacuation orders. In one Spokane neighborhood, blackened vehicles, a boat twisted by the heat and melted plastic recycling bins remained. Across the street, lawns were still green and housed were spared, as residents continued to run hoses or sprinklers to water their properties. Among those who returned were Miriam and Daniel Sim, both 76. Miriam held her hand over her mouth as she surveyed the ruins of the home where they had lived since 2005. "It’s like a war zone,” Miriam said. “There’s nothing to save.” “At our age, do we want to rebuild?” her husband asked. Cpl. Mark Gregory, a spokesman for the Spokane County Sheriff’s Office, said the county initially received nearly 300 reports of missing people, but by Monday they had cleared all but 14. Those outstanding reports more likely represented people who had not been in contact since evacuating than people who were truly missing or in danger, authorities said.

headlines.full_text: Death toll from Venezuela earthquake rises to 6,125 According to a weekly state bulletin, 6,462 people were rescued during search-and-rescue operations CARACAS, August 4. /TASS/. The death toll from the devastating earthquake in Venezuela has risen to 6,125, according to a weekly bulletin published on the Telegram channel of President of the country's National Assembly Jorge Rodriguez. According to the weekly update, 6,462 people were rescued during search-and-rescue operations, 60,992 people received medical treatment, 287 housing units were provided to those left homeless, and 43,679 structures were inspected and assessed, of which 41,624 had sustained damage. The earthquake struck Venezuela on the evening of June 24. Two powerful tremors of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 occurred about 40 seconds apart. Their epicenters were located about 10 km apart in Yaracuy state. The earthquake was followed by over 1,500 aftershocks.

Among the goals of the group – which is dominated by the UK and France – is also to coordinate aid to Kiev. Russia has rejected any unauthorized foreign military presence in Ukraine, suggesting that Western troops would not be“peacekeepers”but rather“occupation forces”and therefore legitimate targets. The Telegraph noted that while new UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham signaled continuity in backing Kiev and NATO, there is no equivalent figure in Paris, with Macron constitutionally required to leave his post after next year’s presidential election. This, the paper added, has sparked concerns about a“slow death”for the coalition. Two potential replacements are Marine Le Pen, leader of the right-wing National Rally, and left-wing firebrand Jean-Luc Melenchon. Both are hardline Ukraine and NATO skeptics. At different times, that “other” has been Byzantium and Eastern Orthodoxy, the Ottoman Empire and the Islamic world, or even Germany, which was once regarded by some as alien to the European spirit. headlines.full_text: Russia has not conveyed signals to West on Ukraine via Kazakhstan — MFA Mikhail Galuzin added that Moscow maintains direct contact with those capable of influencing Kiev ST. PETERSBURG, August 4. /TASS/. The Russian side has not conveyed any signals to the collective West regarding a settlement in Ukraine via Kazakhstan, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin told TASS, adding that Moscow maintains direct contact with those capable of influencing the Kiev regime and sees no need to trouble its Kazakhstani friends with this matter. Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said at a meeting with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin on July 25 that he was receiving numerous signals from Europe and the United States regarding the current state of affairs surrounding the conflict in Ukraine. The Russian leader then briefed his Kazakh counterpart in detail on the current situation regarding Ukraine. Moscow "sees no need to trouble its Kazakhstani friends regarding this matter" or ask them to convey anything to the collective West, Galuzin said on the sidelines of the third Kazakhstan-Russia Media Forum. "We maintain contact and communication directly with those capable of influencing the Kiev regime," he said. "I cannot say that these forces are listening to us closely, but we are continuing our efforts in this direction," the diplomat stressed. The first Media Forum between Russia and Kazakhstan was held at the TASS headquarters in Moscow in November 2024, marking the agency’s 120th anniversary. The second meeting in this format took place last year in Almaty.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article selectively presents information by omitting the signals received by Kazakhstan's President from Europe and the United States, creating a one-sided narrative that downplays the West's involvement in the conflict.

"The seven-year timeframe of new contracts means that the actual increase in output will occur in 2027-2028, not in the coming months. For Ukraine, the impact of the concluded agreements is indirectly rather than directly positive, he noted. headlines.full_text: Nadezhda crew evacuate to Novorossiysk after Ukraine’s drone attack There were 22 crew members on board ISTANBUL, August 3. /TASS/. The crew of the Nadezhda vessel that was attacked by Ukrainian drones near Novorossiysk has been evacuated to the Russian port, Turkey’s Transport Ministry said. "On August 3, 2025, the Ro-Ro-type vessel Nadezhda that was on its way from the port of Novorossiysk to Samsun was reportedly attacked by drones some 20 nautical miles off Novorossiysk’s coast. There were 22 crew members, including 13 Turkish nationals, onboard. Initial reports indicate damage to the ship’s living premises and bow. The fire has not yet been put out," it said. "The crew members have been safely evacuated to the port of Novorossiysk by the Russian naval forces. Initial reports indicate that three crew members may be in critical condition. The fire onboard continues, and the rescue operation is impossible due to ongoing risks of drone attacks in this area," the ministry added. The Cumhuriyet newspaper reported earlier, citing the ship’s captain, that it was attacked by six to seven Ukrainian drones. The 118-meter vessel for the transportation of rolling cargoes Nadezhda (IMO number: 7702657) was built in 1978 in Denmark. According to publicly available data, it is owned by Nadezhda Roro Inc. Its operational and technical manager is Turkish company Kalyoncu Ro Ro Denizcilik.

Save Share Hundreds of unaccompanied minors are stranded in Ceuta in North Africa, following the massive surge of migrants who swam around the border fence with Morocco to reach the Spanish territory. Some of the children are traumatised after witnessing family members drown in the Mediterranean Sea, as tens of thousands left Morocco in search of better opportunities. An estimated 3,000 to 5,000 migrants, of the roughly 60,000 who arrived in Ceuta on Thursday, have avoided expulsion. More than 800 unaccompanied minors are among the remaining migrants and face an uncertain future. A 17-year-old girl from Tangier told the Associated Press she saw Spanish police pulling the body of her eight-year-old brother from the sea when she made it to shore. She was also separated from her mother during the journey. “I saw people stepping on the dead,” she said through a translator. “Now we are children begging on the street.” After finding a government facility for youths in need full, she is now relying on locals for food and shelter. Spanish law says adult migrants can apply for asylum, but the bar is normally set very high for Moroccans to be granted humanitarian protection. If rejected, they will face expulsion procedures. Article 35 of Spain’s 2000 law on foreigners’ rights states that when police identify young children and teenage migrants who are unaccompanied by adults, the minors must be granted protection and receive “immediate attention’ from Spanish child protection services.

headlines.full_text: State Department raises travel warning for part of Spain as migrant surge sparks military deployment Tens of thousands of migrants surged into Spain's Ceuta from Morocco, prompting a military deployment and a new State Department travel advisory. The updated advisory warns that the "massive and uncontrolled arrival of migrants from Morocco to Ceuta may lead to unpredictable and dangerous security situations." "Spain has deployed the Spanish military, Spanish National Police, and Guardia Civil as a result of this serious situation," the advisory states. "Americans should reconsider travel to the area given the risks posed to their safety and security." headlines.full_text: The Migrants Have Left Ceuta, But the Trauma Lingers A city long-known as a melting pot of cultures suddenly feels vulnerable. CEUTA, Spain—By Sunday morning, nearly all of the tens of thousands of migrants who flooded into this tiny Spanish city were gone. But the trauma of the sudden influx lingered. Off a Mediterranean beach, countless shoes bobbed in the blue waters, abandoned by migrantswho had swumto this slice of Spanish territory along the Strait of Gibraltar, just off the coast of Morocco. Evaristo Casares Fernandez, a sanitation worker, noted that it would fall to him to clean up the floating mass of footwear. “It used to be a very tranquil place,” said Casares Fernandez, 55 years old, a Ceuta native. “That’s no longer the case.” For centuries, this city has been a multiethnic melting pot where European and African, Muslim and Christian cultures converged, and coexisted mostly peacefully. Its mix of Spanish military fortifications, churches, mosques and even a synagogue is unusual for North Africa. Now, it is a symbol of the chasm that migration has opened between the two continents. For several chaotic days, migrants flooded into Ceuta, overwhelming the border guards and sending many of the 80,000 permanent residents to the safety of their homes. Shops closed, the enclave’s bustling street life receded. Mercedes Cabrera Lafaro was hoping to reopen her beauty parlor now that the large groups of young men wereno longer roaming the streets. headlines.full_text: 'Your legacy will live forever': Nepal mourns climber Nirmal Purja Tributes are pouring out across Nepal after an avalanche killed some of the country's best mountaineers. Tributes are pouring out across Nepal after an avalanche killed all 10 members of an expedition on Pakistan's Broad Peak, six of whom were Nepalese. Among them wasNirmal Purja, also known as Nims,a British-Nepali climber most known for climbing the world's 14 tallest peaks in just over six months. His death has sent shockwaves through the global mountaineering community and through Nepal, where he is a celebrated figure for giving a spotlight to Nepali climbing guides. Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah was among those who paid tribute, saying his "history of courage, dedication and contribution will always remain inspiring". This year marks the 25th anniversary of the attack, which resulted in nearly 3,000 fatalities and the destruction of the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center in New York City. The annual commemoration is customarily held at the monument built on the spot where the towers used to stand. It is frequented by senior local and federal officials. The upcoming anniversary sparked controversy well before the event, with a group of relatives of the victims launching a petition against Mamdani’s participation. According to the petitioners, the motion has nothing to do with the mayor’s religion, but with his controversial views and perceived connections to radicals. The petition, which was launched last month, reached 50,000 verified signatures earlier this week and over 70,000 as of Sunday. It calls out the Muslim mayor over what it described as“public positions, associations, and responses to rhetoric that many perceive as hostile to these shared values.” Among other things, it listed the mayor’s connections to radical Brooklyn Imam Siraj Wahhaj and the appointment of Ramzi Kassem, who previously represented a terrorist convicted in an Al-Qaeda tanker bombing plot. It made great powers sit down. Under the chairmanship of the Philippines, the 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Manila and its dense constellation of related gatherings turned the capital into one of the few reliable stages where rivals still appear in the same rooms, exchange views, and keep channels open. From July 20 to 24, foreign ministers from Southeast Asia, the United States, China, Russia, Japan, India, Europe, and beyond convened against a distinctly unsettled backdrop of escalating hostilities between the US and Iran and rising tensions between Beijing and the Philippines after incidents in the South China Sea. Yet ASEAN did what it has long done best – it refused to let the friction dictate the terms. The organization offered something that is in very short supply in the modern world of competing geopolitical blocs: a neutral platform where conversation remains possible and practical cooperation continues. Ukraine has been heavily dependent on weapons supplies from its Western backers throughout the conflict, which is now in its fifth year. Moscow has condemned the weapons shipments to Ukraine, arguing that they only prolong the conflict without changing the outcome, and warning that the military assistance shows that NATO is a direct party to the conflict, thereby risking a direct confrontation between Russia and the bloc. The reported plan follows a broader shift in US defense policy under President Donald Trump, whose administration plans to reduce troops and critical weapons systems in Europe and redirect some resources to Asia and other regions. The White House has also pushed NATO members in Europe to take greater responsibility for regional security to significantly raise defense spending. The Security Assistance Group-Ukraine (SAG-U), based in the German city of Wiesbaden, coordinates weapons deliveries, training and logistical support for Ukraine. Strongest quake in 40 years rocks Italy’s volcanic region, injures dozens (VIDEOS) At least 26 people have been injured after the strongest earthquake in four decades struck Italy’s Campi Flegrei volcanic area near Naples
Read Full Article at RT.com A magnitude 4.7 earthquake struck the Campi Flegrei volcanic region near Naples in southern Italy on Friday evening, injuring at least 26 people, two of them critically, and damaging dozens of buildings. The earthquake hit at 7:46pm local time at a shallow depth of about 3km, according to Italy’s National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology (INGV). Its epicenter was between the towns of Pozzuoli and Quarto. Civil protection officials said that it was the strongest quake recorded in the area since continuous instrumental monitoring began, surpassing two magnitude 4.6 tremors registered in 2025. The quake was felt across Naples, Ischia, Procida, and much of the Gulf of Naples. Seismographs have since recorded more than 60 aftershocks, the strongest measuring magnitude 3.8 late on Friday and another of 3.1 early on Saturday. Civil Protection Minister Nello Musumeci warned that the seismic swarm is continuing and that further earthquakes above magnitude 3 remain possible. The worst damage was reported in Pozzuoli, where falling masonry, collapsing facades, and landslides damaged homes, businesses, and parked vehicles, according to multiple videos posted online. headlines.full_text: Amur tiger cubs transferred by Russia to Kazakhstan could be released into wild in year The cubs need to reach the age of 18 months, Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Ecology says ASTANA, August 4. /TASS/. Amur tiger cubs transferred by Russia to Kazakhstan will remain in captivity for about another year, until they reach the age of 18 months, Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Ecology announced. The tiger cubs arrived in the republic in May at the age of 6-7 months, the ministry said, adding that they continue to grow and develop in specially equipped enclosures at the Ile-Balkhash State Nature Reserve in southern Kazakhstan. "They will remain under the supervision of specialists until they reach the age of 18 months," the ministry stated. Specialists will decide whether each tiger cub can be released into the wild following veterinary examinations and behavioral tests. Moreover, a male tiger remains under constant observation. "A decision regarding his release into the wild will be made once all tests are complete and his readiness for independent life has been confirmed," the ministry noted. In May, four Amur tigers were transported from Khabarovsk to the Ile-Balkhash Nature Reserve. They are the closest relatives of Caspian tigers, which used to inhabit Central Asia. In Kazakhstan, they went extinct by 1948. The country expects that the special program will help revive their population.

headlines.full_text: NATO command responsible for coordinating arms supplies to Kiev remains in US hands The process of transferring command positions in Europe to European generals did not affect this command structure of the alliance BRUSSELS, August 3. /TASS/. The NATO command in Wiesbaden for coordinating military supplies to Ukraine (NSATU) is now headed by US Army Lieutenant General Guillaume Beaurpere, who has taken the reins from Lieutenant General Curtis Bazzard, said chair of the NATO Military Committee, Admiral Giuseppe Cavo Dragone. Thus, the process of transferring command positions in Europe to European generals, which the United States and NATO said would be launched this year, did not affect this command structure of the alliance. "Today, at Clay Kaserne in Wiesbaden NATO Security Assistance and Training for Ukraine changes command," he wrote on X. "To Lieutenant General Guillaume Beaurpere: welcome! You take charge of a mission that matters." Cavo Dragone noted the particular importance of NSATU for NATO. "We imagined the wars of this century as bits and bytes. What we are watching is different: masses and machines together - soldiers, artillery, logistics under fire, married to cheap, fast, tactically decisive solutions and uncrewed systems, and applied AI iterating in weeks, not procurement cycles. NSATU sits where that knowledge is generated, and it feeds both our strategic commands," he said. NSATU began to be hastily created virtually immediately after Donald Trump’s victory in the US elections to ensure coordination of military supplies to the Kiev regime in case Trump cuts aid to Kiev.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article selectively presents information about NATO command structure, omitting opposing facts that might contradict the narrative that the US still maintains control over key command positions.

Observations from the CMA's national climate center show that the central and eastern equatorial Pacific reached the threshold for El Nino conditions in May, and sea surface temperatures in the region continued to rise in June.
